source_text: Τοῦτο δὴ τοῦθ᾽ οὕτως ἔχειν νομίσας, ἔγνων ἐπὶ ἑτέραν ἰδέαν τραπέσθαι βίου, καὶ ἐκδοῦναι μὲν ἐμαυτὸν τρυφῇ, πεῖραν δὲ λαβεῖν ἡδονῶν ποικίλων. Νῦν τοίνυν συνῆκα ὡς τὰ τοιαῦτα μάταια σύμπαντα· καὶ γέλωτα μὲν εἰκῆ φερόμενον ἐπέσχον, ἡδονὴν δὲ πρὸς τὸ σωφρονεῖν ἐκόλασα, πικρῶς ἐπιτιμήσας αὐτῇ. Λογισάμενος δέ, ὅτι ψυχὴ δύναται στῆσαι μεθύουσαν καὶ ῥέουσαν ὥσπερ οἶνον σώματος φύσιν, ἐγκράτεια δὲ δουλοῦται ἐπιθυμίαν· προεθυμήθην κατιδεῖν, τί ποτε εἴη προκείμενον ἀνθρώποις σπουδαῖον, καὶ τῷ ὄντι καλὸν ὃ καταπράξονται παρὰ τουτονὶ τὸν βίον. Διεξελήλυθα γὰρ τὰ λοιπὰ σύμπαντα ὅσ᾽ ἀξιάγαστα νομίζεται, οἴκων τε ὑπερυψήλων ἀνορθώσεις καὶ φυτείας ἀμπέλων, ἔτι δὲ παραδείσων κατασκευάς, καὶ παντοίων δένδρων καρποφόρων κτήσεις καὶ ἐπιμελείας· ὅπου δὲ καὶ δεξαμεναὶ μεγάλαι πρὸς ὑποδοχὰς ὑδάτων κατεσκευάσθησαν, εἰς δαψιλῆ ἀρδείαν τῶν φυτῶν ἀπονενεμημέναι. Περιεβαλόμην δὲ καὶ οἰκετῶν πλῆθος, θεράποντας καὶ θεραπαίνας· ἄλλους μὲν ἔξωθεν κτησάμενος, ἄλλους δὲ καὶ παρ᾽ ἐμαυτῷ γενομένους καρπωσάμενος. Ζώων δὲ τετραπόδων ἀγέλαι, πολλαὶ μὲν βουκολίων, πολλαὶ δὲ ποιμνίων ὑπὸ τὴν ἐμὴν ἦλθον ἐξουσίαν παρ᾽ ὁντινοῦν τῶν πάλαι. Θησαυροί τε χρυσοῦ τε καὶ ἀργύρου προσέρρεον, δορυφόρους τέ μοι καὶ δασμοφόρους, τοὺς ἁπάντων βασιλεῖς πεποιημένῳ. Χοροί τε συνεκροτοῦντο παμπληθεῖς, ἀρρένων δέ τε ὁμοῦ καὶ θηλειῶν εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν τέρψιν, παναρμόνιον ἐκπονούντων ᾠδήν. Συμπόσιά γε μὴν καὶ οἰνοχόους εἰς τοῦτο ἀπέταξα τῆς τρυφῆς μέρος ἐξ ἑκατέρου γένους ἀνθρώπων ἐξειλεγμένους, οὐδ᾽ ἂν καταλέγειν ἔχοιμι, τοσοῦτον ὑπερέβαλον τούτοις τοὺς πρὸ ἐμοῦ βασιλεύσαντας Ἱερουσαλήμ. Εἶτα συνέβαινε, τὰ μὲν τῆς σοφίας μοι ἐλαττοῦσθαι, πληθύνειν δὲ τὰ τῆς οὐκ ἀγαθῆς ἐπιθυμίας. Παντὶ γὰρ ὀφθαλμῶν τε δελεάσματι, καὶ καρδίας ἀκράτοις ὁρμαῖς ἐφιεὶς πανταχόθεν προσπιπτούσαις, ἡδονῶν ἐλπίσιν ἐμαυτὸν ἐκδεδωκώς· καὶ πάσαις τρυφαῖς δειλαίαις, τὴν ἐμαυτοῦ ἐγκατέδησα προαίρεσιν. Οὕτω γάρ μου αἱ ἐνθυμήσεις, εἰς δυσπραγίαν ἠνέχθησαν, ὡς ταῦτα μὲν εἶναι καλά, ταῦτα δέ μοι προσήκειν διαπράττεσθαι νομίζειν. Εἶτα ποτὲ ἀνανήψας ἐγὼ καὶ ἀναβλέψας, κατεῖδον ἅπερ ἐν χερσὶν εἶχον, μοχθηρὰ ὁμοῦ καὶ παγχάλεπα, πνεύματος οὐκ ἀγαθοῦ ποιήματα. Οὐδὲν γὰρ ὁτιοῦν ὑπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων ᾑρημένον, ἀποδεκτὸν εἶναί μοι νῦν καταφαίνεται καὶ περισπούδαστον ὀρθῷ λογισμῷ.
thought_title: Solomon tries pleasure and great works
orientation: Solomon tries luxury, great buildings, servants, wealth and music, then comes to his senses and sees them as wretched.
pass_a_gloss: Having thought that this very thing is so, I determined to turn to another form of life, and to hand myself over to luxury, and to take trial of varied pleasures. Now then I understood that all such things are vain; and laughter borne along at random I checked, and pleasure I chastised toward being temperate, having rebuked it bitterly. And having reckoned that a soul is able to make stand the nature of the body, drunken and flowing like wine, and that self-mastery enslaves desire, I was eager to look into what serious, worthwhile thing is set before human beings, and in reality good, which they will accomplish during this present life. For I have gone through all the remaining things that are considered admirable: erections of very lofty houses and plantings of vines, and further constructions of parks/gardens, and acquisitions and cultivations of fruit-bearing trees of all kinds; where also great reservoirs were constructed for receiving waters, assigned to abundant watering of the plants. And I put around myself a multitude of household slaves, male servants and female servants, some acquired from outside, others born in my house whose fruit I enjoyed. Herds of four-footed animals, many of cattle, many of flocks, came under my authority, beyond anyone at all of those of old. Treasures of gold and silver flowed toward me, who had made the kings of all both spear-bearers and tribute-bearers to me. Choruses very numerous were assembled, of males and females together, for my delight, working out an all-harmonious song. Banquets indeed and wine-pourers chosen out from each sex, whom I appointed to this part of luxury, I could not even enumerate, so greatly did I exceed in these those who reigned over Jerusalem before me. Then it came about that the things of wisdom were diminished for me, and the things of a not-good desire multiplied. For yielding to every bait of the eyes and to unmixed, unrestrained impulses of the heart falling upon me from every side, I had given myself over to hopes of pleasures; and to all wretched luxuries I bound fast my own choice. For thus my thoughts were carried into misfortune, so as to think that these things are good and that it befits me to carry them out. Then at some time having become sober again and having looked up, I perceived what I had in hands: things wretched and very grievous together, makings of a not-good spirit. For nothing whatever chosen by human beings now appears to me acceptable and much to be striven for to right reasoning.

pass_b_english: Judging that this was indeed so, I resolved to turn to another way of life: to give myself over to luxury and to make trial of pleasures of many kinds (Ecclesiastes 2:1). Now I have understood that all such things are vain. I held back laughter that ran on without reason, and I disciplined pleasure into sobriety, rebuking it sharply (Ecclesiastes 2:2). And reasoning that the soul can steady the body's nature when it is drunk and flowing like wine, and that self-control makes desire its slave, I was eager to see what worthy thing is set before human beings, what is truly good, that they may accomplish in this present life (Ecclesiastes 2:3).

For I went through everything else that people think admirable. I raised lofty houses and planted vineyards (Ecclesiastes 2:4); I laid out gardens and acquired and tended fruit trees of every kind (Ecclesiastes 2:5); great pools were built to hold water, set apart to water the plants abundantly (Ecclesiastes 2:6). I gathered about me a crowd of household servants, men and women, some acquired from outside, others born in my own house whose service I enjoyed (Ecclesiastes 2:7). Herds of four-footed beasts, many herds of cattle and many flocks of sheep, came under my control, more than anyone of old had possessed (Ecclesiastes 2:7). Treasures of gold and silver flowed in to me, for I had made the kings of all peoples my guards and my tributaries (Ecclesiastes 2:8). Great choirs of men and women together were gathered for my delight, performing songs in perfect harmony (Ecclesiastes 2:8). As for banquets, and the cupbearers chosen from men and women alike whom I assigned to this side of luxury, I could not even count them, so far did I surpass in these things those who had reigned in Jerusalem before me (Ecclesiastes 2:8-9).

Then it happened that my wisdom grew less, while desire that is not good increased. For I gave way to every lure of the eyes and to the unchecked impulses of the heart that pressed on me from every side (Ecclesiastes 2:10); I surrendered myself to the hope of pleasures, and I tied my own will fast to every wretched luxury. For so far had my thoughts been carried toward ruin that I believed these things were good and that it was right for me to pursue them. Then at last I came to my senses and lifted my eyes, and I saw what I had in my hands: things wretched and utterly grievous, the works of a spirit that is not good (Ecclesiastes 2:11). For now nothing at all that human beings choose appears to me, by right reason, worth accepting or worth pursuing with zeal.
notes: Paraphrase of Ecclesiastes 2:1-11. 'Then it happened that my wisdom grew less' deliberately reverses Ecclesiastes 2:9b ('my wisdom remained with me'); Gregory reads Solomon's experiment as a fall, so that clause is left uncited to avoid presenting it as the verse's sense. The cupbearers 'from men and women alike' follow the LXX of 2:8 (οἰνοχόον καὶ οἰνοχόας). In 2:8 'the kings of all peoples' supplies 'peoples' for the bare genitive ἁπάντων ('of all'). 'Will' renders προαίρεσις (deliberate choice). 'A spirit that is not good' (πνεύματος οὐκ ἀγαθοῦ) again turns the LXX 'choice of spirit' (2:11) into an evil spirit; kept lower case. The choirs clause renders the men and women singers of 2:8 and is cited to that verse. No doubtful readings in the copy-text.
